record.paper_title: Results and Open Questions on the Boundary Control of Moving Sets
record.original_question: Let t→Ω(t)⊂R^2 be a moving set with C^1 boundary and inward normal speed β(t,x)≥β*. Suppose there are controls α^ε≥0 and solutions u^ε of the rescaled reaction-diffusion equation u_t^ε=(1/ε)f(u^ε)+εΔu^ε-αu^ε such that u^ε(t,·) converges in L^1 to the indicator function 1_{Ω(t)} for every t∈[0,T]. Must the control costs satisfy the lower bound lim inf_{ε→0} ∫_{R^2} α^ε(t,x) dx ≥ ∫_{∂Ω(t)} E(β(t,x)) dσ? Equivalently, can one prove the converse inequality needed to justify the moving-set cost functional as a Γ-limit of the rescaled parabolic control costs?

evidence.quote: In view of these results, one may speculate if it is possible to regard the cost functional J as a Γ-limit of the functionals J^ε. Toward this goal, one would need a converse to Theorem 3.1.

Question 1: In the same setting of Theorem 3.1, consider any family of control functions α^ε ≥ 0 and corresponding solutions u^ε to (3.6) such that (3.7) holds. Does this imply that lim inf_{ε→0} ∫_{R2} α^ε(t, x) dx ≥ ∫_{∂Ω(t)} E(β(t, x)) dσ ? (3.10)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setting. Let f∈C^2(R) be a bistable reaction term with f(0)=f(1)=0, f'(0)<0, f'(1)<0, and ∫_0^1 f(s)ds>0, so that there exists a unique traveling-wave profile U:R→(0,1) with U(-∞)=1, U(+∞)=0 and traveling speed c*>0 solving U''+c*U'+f(U)=0. For each β≥0, let U_β be the unique profile and let E(β)≥0 denote the corresponding minimal asymptotic "control density" (per unit length of interface) needed for a planar interface to advance at inward normal speed β; concretely E is the convex, monotone function arising from the one-dimensional control problem
    min ∫_R α(x) U_β(x) dx
subject to the existence of a profile U_β satisfying U_β'' + β U_β' + f(U_β) − α U_β = 0 with U_β(-∞)=1, U_β(+∞)=0, α≥0.

Problem. Let T>0 and let t↦Ω(t)⊂R^2, t∈[0,T], be a moving open set with C^1 boundary whose inward normal speed β(t,x) at x∈∂Ω(t) satisfies β(t,x)≥β_* for some β_*>0. Consider a family of nonnegative measurable controls α^ε:[0,T]×R^2→[0,∞) and corresponding classical solutions u^ε:[0,T]×R^2→R of the rescaled reaction-diffusion equation
    u^ε_t = (1/ε) f(u^ε) + ε Δ u^ε − α^ε u^ε  on (0,T)×R^2,
with 0≤u^ε≤1, such that for every t∈[0,T] one has u^ε(t,·) → 1_{Ω(t)} in L^1(R^2) as ε→0.

Prove or disprove: for almost every t∈[0,T],
    liminf_{ε→0} ∫_{R^2} α^ε(t,x) dx  ≥  ∫_{∂Ω(t)} E(β(t,x)) dσ(x).

Equivalently, establish the Γ-liminf inequality that, together with the known Γ-limsup (recovery sequence) construction, would identify the moving-set boundary cost functional J(Ω,β)=∫_0^T ∫_{∂Ω(t)} E(β(t,x)) dσ dt as the Γ-limit of the rescaled parabolic control cost functionals J^ε(α^ε)=∫_0^T ∫_{R^2} α^ε(t,x) dx dt.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an explicit open problem in a 2025 survey by A. Bressan on boundary control of moving sets, asking for the converse (Γ-liminf) inequality to a known one-sided bound. No published resolution of the converse sharp-interface lower bound for this rescaled reaction-diffusion control problem appears in the literature search.

status_evidence.title: Results and open questions on the boundary control of moving sets
status_evidence.snippet: Survey listing open questions including the converse to the sharp-interface lower bound on control cost.
status_evidence.claim: The converse inequality needed for the Γ-limit identification is stated as an open question.

status_evidence.title: Optimal control of moving sets
status_evidence.snippet: Earlier paper establishing the direct (one-sided) sharp-interface bound, motivating but not resolving the converse.
status_evidence.claim: Only the direct inequality and recovery sequence are established in the prior literature.
